Subject: Dedicated sizing ask — 13B / 32k usage profile and quant impact

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are close to committing but need an engineering-side sizing confirmation before procurement. Quick background: our production workload will use a 13B model variant with 32k max context (mix of 2k–32k requests, ~20% at >16k), average qps target 70 peak, avg response length ~600 tokens. We plan to use streaming for final responses.

Questions we need answered for our procurement:
- Rough committed GPU count for a Dedicated pool to meet 70 peak qps with ~99th percentile latency target of 300ms for <=4k requests, and graceful degradation above that.
- Footprint per pod depending on precision: FP16 vs 4-bit (nf4) weights, and assumptions about KV cache placement (on-GPU vs NVMe offload).
- Whether we can hit a single A100-80GB per inferentia/pod with quant + KV offload, or need multi-GPU tiling.

I can share sample traces; attaching our simplified tail/peak trace. Can we get a short write-up we can share with procurement (including numbers we can put into our CAPEX request)?

Appreciate it — Elena
Elena Torres
VP ML Platform, Aurelius Labs
(elena@aureliuslabs.ai)

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — 13B / 32k usage profile and quant impact

Thanks Elena — pulled your trace and ran a quick pass. Summary up-front (full breakdown attached):

Key assumptions used in the attached spreadsheet (precision-scaling.xlsx):
- Model: open-13B-32k (weight footprint approximations)
- Request mix: 60% <4k, 20% 4k–16k, 20% 16k–32k (matches your sample)
- Avg response 600 tokens (streaming), token generation on GPU
- Concurrency policy: continuous batching + max batch latency 40ms

High-level numbers (per-pod GPU memory footprint if KV cache kept on GPU):
- FP16 weights: ~26 GB (weights + optimizer-free overhead)
- KV cache (full 32k): ~58 GB (approx 1.8 MB per token * 32k => ~58 GB)
- Total (FP16 + KV full): ~84 GB => does NOT fit comfortably on a single 80GB A100; would require model sharding or multi-GPU tiling.

With 4-bit (nf4) quantization for weights (no KV quant):
- Quant weights: ~11 GB
- KV cache (full 32k): ~58 GB
- Total: ~69 GB => fits on an 80GB card but with limited headroom for batching and ROS/serving overhead.

KV offload option (recommended for committed pool):
- Keep model weights and short-term KV on GPU; stream long KV pages to NVMe (we support async KV offload in Dedicated).
- On-GPU working set: quant weights (~11 GB) + hot KV window (configurable, e.g., last 4k tokens ~7 GB) + OS/runtime ~6–8 GB => total ~25–27 GB, comfortable on 80GB for batching headroom.

Throughput / fleet sizing (back-of-envelope for 70 peak qps):
- Single 80GB pod (quant + KV offload) estimated steady-state throughput: ~8–10 effective seq/s * concurrency policies -> roughly 7–9 inference QPS for avg response length/streaming profile.
- Conservatively, we recommend 9 pods per 100 QPS of similar workload to maintain 99th percentile targets and allow for headroom and canaries.

Recommended committed pool for procurement (initial):
- 12 x A100-80GB (Dedicated) with KV offload enabled, autoscale + 3 extra for maintenance/canary (total pool size 15).
- Rationale: supports 70 peak qps with buffer for bursty 32k requests, ability to test rolling quantized model variants, and isolation (we did the math for conversion to other instance families if needed).

Attached: precision-scaling.xlsx (breakdowns + sensitivity for 0–32k split), kv_sim_results.csv (sim traces & numbers). Next steps: if you want we can run a short validation using your trace on our preprod cluster (2–3 hour run) to confirm p95/p99.

--

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing ask — practical options and rollout plan

Elena — quick operational notes and an alternative path we often use that reduces upfront GPU commitment: 

Option A (Tessa's recommendation): committed 12–15 A100-80GB with KV offload. Pros: predictability, single-tenant performance SLAs, simple fallback policies. Cons: higher commitment.

Option B (Cost-hedged rollout): start with 8 committed A100-80GB + burstable pool (on-demand) + early model quantization canary (nf4) for 10% traffic. Practical steps:
- Week 0–1: deploy quantized variant behind a canary route (10% traffic), KV offload enabled. Observe p95/p99 and cost delta.
- Week 2: if p99 within 2x target or better, bump to 30% and run load test (we can synthetic-load using your traces).
- Week 3–4: scale committed capacity to desired steady level based on validated quant benefits (we often see 30–45% GPU reduction for 13B with nf4 + KV offload).

A few operational caveats:
- Cold-start KV offload can add tail latency spikes; we mitigate with warmup prefetch policies and small GPU-resident hot-window.
- We recommend pinning a fallback (fp16) model for critical endpoints to avoid regressions during canary.

If you want, Marcus and I can run the 2–3 hour preprod run Tessa mentioned and then present a one-page procurement-ready summary with clear numbers and minimal jargon.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise SE, Redwood Inference
